title: FTX: Customers Got 105% Back. Why He Still Got 25 Years
summary:
FTX collapse explained from the court, SEC and bankruptcy records.

FTX customers have now been repaid 105% of their claims, yet Sam Bankman-Fried is serving 25 years. Using the Second Circuit's June 2026 opinion, the US Attorney's releases, the SEC's complaint, John J. Ray III's sworn bankruptcy declaration, the Delaware bankruptcy court's rulings, the FTX Recovery Trust's distribution notices and the Supreme Court docket, we explain the code privileges, the nine-day run, the trial, the repayments, why claims were fixed at November 2022 prices, and why the courts said repayment does not undo fraud. SEC claims are allegations; the criminal findings are the jury's and the courts'. The Supreme Court has not decided whether to hear his petition.

Chapter one. Two companies, one owner.

scenes.say: FTX was a crypto exchange. Sam Bankman-Fried ran it as chief executive from its founding in twenty nineteen.

visual.text: FTX founded, Bankman-Fried CEO from the start

scenes.say: He also controlled a trading firm, Alameda Research, founded in twenty seventeen and co-owned with FTX's co-founder, Gary Wang.

Wang: FTX co-founder and chief technology officer

scenes.say: The appeals court describes Alameda as FTX's largest customer and primary market maker.

visual.text: Alameda was FTX's largest customer and primary market maker.

scenes.say: So the people who ran the exchange also owned its biggest trader. That is where this story starts.

visual.text: One owner. Both sides of the trade.

scenes.say: At trial, Gary Wang described special privileges built into FTX's code for Alameda.

visual.header: Gary Wang's testimony and the court's summary, 2d Cir.

lines: Alameda allowed negative balances on FTX's books
!A $65 billion line of credit it could draw from FTX

visual.label: line of credit Alameda could draw from FTX

scenes.say: The SEC alleged Alameda was also exempted from certain key FTX risk mitigation measures.

scenes.say: After the verdict, prosecutors said he directed co-conspirators to alter FTX's code so Alameda could withdraw effectively unlimited amounts of crypto.

visual.text: …to alter FTX's computer code to allow Alameda to withdraw effectively unlimited amounts of cryptocurrency from the exchange.

scenes.say: Since at least May twenty nineteen, the SEC said, FTX raised more than one point eight billion dollars from equity investors.

scenes.say: The SEC's complaint says Bankman-Fried promoted FTX as a safe, responsible crypto asset trading platform, with sophisticated, automated risk measures to protect customer assets.

visual.title: What investors were told (SEC complaint)

Alameda exempted from key risk measures

scenes.say: Chapter three. Nine days in November.

visual.text: Nine days in November

scenes.say: On the second of November twenty twenty-two, a crypto news site published a version of Alameda's balance sheet.

visual.text: A version of Alameda's balance sheet is published

scenes.say: The appeals court says that triggered widespread customer withdrawals from FTX.
On the eleventh of November, Bankman-Fried was replaced and FTX filed for bankruptcy. It could no longer meet customers' withdrawal requests.

lines: Bankman-Fried replaced as CEO
!FTX files for bankruptcy: unable to meet withdrawal requests

scenes.say: At his trial, Bankman-Fried testified that he was surprised to learn of Alameda's eight billion dollar negative balance on FTX in October twenty twenty-two.

visual.label: Alameda's negative balance on FTX, October 2022

scenes.say: The new chief executive was John J. Ray the third, who had worked on the clean-up of Enron.
Six days later he filed a sworn declaration. He wrote: never in my career have I seen such a complete failure of corporate controls.

visual.text: Never in my career have I seen such a complete failure of corporate controls …
visual.by: John J. Ray III, declaration, 17 Nov 2022

scenes.say: He described the absence of an accurate list of bank accounts and signatories, and said the group did not keep centralised control of its cash.

lines: No accurate list of bank accounts and signatories
!No centralised control of cash
Corporate funds used to buy homes for employees and advisors

scenes.say: Corporate money, he said, had bought homes and other personal items for employees and advisors. Some payments were approved by responding with personalised emojis.

visual.label: how some disbursements were approved, per the Ray declaration

scenes.say: And Bankman-Fried, he said, used messaging apps set to auto-delete after a short period of time, and encouraged employees to do the same.

visual.text: applications that were set to auto-delete after a short period of time, and encouraged employees to do the same
visual.by: John J. Ray III, declaration, 17 Nov 2022

scenes.say: Chapter four. The verdict.

visual.text: The verdict

scenes.say: The trial in Manhattan ran four weeks. Three of his inner circle testified under cooperation agreements: Caroline Ellison, Gary Wang, and FTX's former head of engineering, Nishad Singh.

visual.title: Cooperating witnesses
items: Caroline Ellison, former CEO of Alameda
Nishad Singh, former FTX head of engineering

scenes.say: On the second of November twenty twenty-three, the jury convicted him on all seven counts of fraud and conspiracy.

visual.title: 2 November 2023
visual.src: 2d Cir. opinion, 12 Jun 2026; US Attorney SDNY, 28 Mar 2024

scenes.src: 2d Cir. opinion, 12 Jun 2026; US Attorney SDNY, 28 Mar 2024

scenes.say: The US Attorney, Damian Williams, said the industry might be new, but, in his words, this kind of corruption is as old as time.

visual.text: …this kind of corruption is as old as time.

scenes.say: On the twenty-eighth of March twenty twenty-four, Judge Lewis Kaplan sentenced him to twenty-five years, with forfeiture of more than eleven billion dollars.

visual.text: 25 years in prison, over $11bn forfeiture

scenes.say: Prosecutors put the losses at more than eight billion dollars of customers' money, one point seven billion from FTX investors, and one point three billion from Alameda's lenders.
The defence argued customers had lost no money. Reuters reported that the judge called that misleading, logically flawed and speculative.

visual.text: …misleading, it is logically flawed, it is speculative.
visual.by: Judge Lewis A. Kaplan, as reported by Reuters

scenes.say: He compared it to a thief who takes his loot to Las Vegas and wins. Repaying the loss from the winnings, he said, earns no discount.

visual.text: Stolen money, bet in Las Vegas
visual.sub: Winning the bet earns no sentencing discount

scenes.say: Chapter five. The money comes back.

visual.text: The money comes back

scenes.say: In October twenty twenty-four, the Delaware bankruptcy court confirmed FTX's repayment plan, with between fourteen point seven and sixteen point five billion dollars to distribute.

visual.text: Plan confirmed: $14.7bn to $16.5bn to distribute

scenes.say: FTX said ninety-eight per cent of its creditors, by number, would receive about one hundred and nineteen per cent of their allowed claims.

Then came the payments. After the fourth round, in March twenty twenty-six, international customers were at ninety-six per cent. The fifth round, in July, took both customer classes to one hundred and five.

scenes.say: Chapter six. The appeal.

visual.text: The appeal

scenes.say: Bankman-Fried appealed. On the twelfth of June twenty twenty-six, a three-judge panel of the Second Circuit affirmed the conviction, the sentence and the forfeiture.

visual.title: Second Circuit, No. 24-961
items: Opinion by Judge Barrington D. Parker

scenes.say: One of his central complaints was evidence the jury never heard: that customers would be repaid, and that his investments later rose in value.

visual.text: They were going to be repaid (his argument)

scenes.say: Here is the sentence we promised. FTX customers were defrauded as soon as Bankman-Fried transferred their money to Alameda.

visual.text: FTX customers were defrauded as soon as Bankman-Fried transferred their money to Alameda
visual.by: US Court of Appeals, Second Circuit, 12 Jun 2026

scenes.say: The trial judge had ruled it immaterial as a matter of law whether he intended to repay. The appeals court agreed, and said the law covers even temporary misappropriation.

visual.title: Why repayment did not matter
lines: !Trial judge: intent to repay 'immaterial as a matter of law' (upheld)
The statute encompasses temporary misappropriation

scenes.say: Whether the assets he bought appreciated in value, the judges wrote, is irrelevant as to whether he committed fraud.

visual.label: whether the assets he bought rose in value, the court held

scenes.say: And they described him using FTX as his own personal piggy bank, spending customer funds on real estate, political contributions and investments.

visual.text: using FTX as his own personal piggy bank
visual.by: US Court of Appeals, Second Circuit, 12 Jun 2026

scenes.say: It is not over. On the tenth of September, he asked the US Supreme Court to hear his case.

visual.text: Petition to the US Supreme Court, No. 26-349

scenes.say: Five amicus briefs followed in October, one from a group of bankruptcy law professors. The government's response is due on the sixteenth of December. The justices have not yet decided whether to take the case.

visual.title: Supreme Court docket 26-349
